coverage.design_evaluation_explanation: Matches 3 of 6 ground-truth variable items (50%): the TorchOpt-versus-autograd comparison, computation-time measurement, and numerical-stability evaluation using gradient comparisons and convergence criteria. Timing covers forward and backward work, although it aggregates them into outer-iteration latency.
coverage.design_error_analysis: The design restricts execution to CPU instead of varying CPU, GPU, and distributed multi-GPU, and replaces ResNet18/ResNet50 with toy workloads. Although initialization and some settings are matched across arms, it does not establish the required fixed Adam optimizer and batch size, and learning rate is a manipulated variable. Forward and backward durations are not recorded separately.
coverage.conclusion_evaluation_explanation: The conclusion output is empty, so it does not semantically match the ground-truth conclusion.
coverage.conclusion_error_analysis: No conclusion states that TorchOpt should reduce computation and enhance numerical stability, experimentally verifiable through time and memory comparisons against traditional back-propagation.
